# NET-006: DOCKER-USER chain state

- **Group:** Firewall and exposure
- **Severity when it fails:** info
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check may report `unknown`; it never reports a pass it could not verify.

## Why it matters

Docker's published ports are forwarded before UFW's input rules see them; the DOCKER-USER chain is the one place iptables lets you filter them. This records whether the chain is absent, default (no filtering) or filtered, and which firewall backend Docker programs, for DKR-001 and NET-007.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER; sudo nft list tables
```

## How to fix it

No direct fix: filter published ports in DOCKER-USER (ufw-docker does this) or publish them on 127.0.0.1 only.

Run `stackward explain NET-006` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
